A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Draft and Refine (DnR) work. All 11 pages in each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original DnR experiments across multimodal benchmarks, hallucination evaluations and expert-selection efficiency comparisons in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, hallucination and expert-selection results in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same relevance maps, probabilistic masking, utilization score, expert rendering and selection procedures, including the learned selector and its objective.

E1.justification: The same 16 multimodal benchmarks appear in Table 1. The hallucination evaluation retains HaloQuest, MMHal-Bench, VizWiz and COCO Caption, with no added or removed task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same seven LVLM Draft/DnR comparisons. Table 3 retains the exhaustive versus policy-driven selection comparison using PaliGemma.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged, including 16 masks per image, Top-k/Bottom-k masking ratios of 0.25/0.75, GRAY rendering with Hybrid masking for comprehensive evaluation, and highlight rendering for hallucination evaluation.

E4.justification: The relevance-map and rendering illustrations, utilization–accuracy correlation analyses, failure-case discussions and expert-selection efficiency study are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Pearson/Spearman correlation reporting and stochastic-mask sampling information are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and reported qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains PaliGemma VQAv2 exhaustive/policy-driven scores of 75.2/74.9 and the average cost change of -70.39%.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including relevance aggregation, masking probabilities, adaptive weighting, utilization and selector loss, are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about utilization-guided expert coordination, improved visual grounding, accuracy and reduced hallucination. The added code-access statement does not revise these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including explanations of VizWiz and Flickr degradations, inability to supply missing conceptual knowledge, and sensitivity to rendering and heuristic masking in Section 5.

D1.justification: v3 adds 'Code is available at Github' to the abstract, with a repository hyperlink absent from v1. This adds implementation-access information; technical settings and implementation descriptions otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 77 cited works are unchanged. The repository hyperlink is an implementation-access addition, not a new research citation.

P1.justification: v3 adds one short code-availability sentence and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording, terminology and section organization are unchanged after matching text across page breaks.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes limited text reflow across pages 1–3. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–3 retain their content and presentation; pages 4–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository link supplies an implementation-access pointer missing from v1, providing a limited reproducibility and usability benefit. Scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, but not the repository's completeness or functionality.
